issues.body:
## Goal

One layer for campaign e2e that lets a test (a) **synthesise any campaign state directly** and (b) **move between named milestones, asserting the state at each** — so a test says "day 12, Drassen held at 70 %, 120k funds, four mercs" instead of replaying the UI to get there.

The tactical track already proved the pattern with `BattleScenario.cc` / `ja2.debug("battle", spec)`. This is the strategic analogue: it mutates the **live** campaign globals (no parallel state), so a save taken after staging is a real, save-game-compatible save.

## Part 1 — state authoring (save-compatible)

The harness mutates the live campaign globals that `SaveLoadGame.cc` writes. No new save format, no fixture blob:

| State | Globals | Serialised by |
|---|---|---|
| money | `LaptopSaveInfo.iCurrentBalance` | `SaveLaptopInfoToSavedGame` |
| day / time | `guiDay`, `guiHour`, `guiMin` (world clock) | `SaveGeneralInfo` / clock |
| difficulty | `gGameOptions.ubDifficultyLevel` (1..3) | game options |
| sector control / garrison | `StrategicMap[].fEnemyControlled`, `SectorInfo[].ubNumAdmins/Troops/Elites` (+ `*InBattle`) | `SaveStrategicInfoToSavedFile`, `LoadSaveSectorInfo` |
| town loyalty / militia | `gTownLoyalty[].ubRating/fStarted`, `SectorInfo[].ubNumberOfCivsAtLevel[]`, `gfTownUsesLoyalty` | `SaveStrategicTownLoyaltyToSaveGameFile` |
| merc roster | `gMercProfiles[].bMercStatus/sSector/bAssignment`, team list (`HireMerc`, `AddSoldierToTeamAndMinimap`) | `SaveMercProfiles`, `SaveSoldierStructure` |
| per-merc inventory | `SOLDIERTYPE.inv[]` (`CreateItems` / `AutoPlaceObject`) | `SaveSoldierStructure` |
| progress | `gubQuest[]`, `gubFact[]` (`SetFactTrue`, `SetQuest`) | `SaveStrategicStatusToSaveGameFile` |

**The contract is proven by a round trip:** stage → `ja2.save("fixture")` → `ja2.load("fixture")` → `ja2.state()` / view models unchanged.

New `src/game/Automation/CampaignScenario.{h,cc}`, wired as `ja2.debug("campaign", spec)` — same shape and conventions as `BattleScenario`:

```lua
ja2.debug("campaign", {
  day = 12, hour = 9, minute = 0,       -- world clock
  money = 120000,
  difficulty = 2,                        -- 1..3
  towns = {                              -- keyed by town id or name
    ["Drassen"] = { owned = true, loyalty = 70, militia = { green = 5, regular = 3, elite = 1 } },
  },
  sectors = {                            -- "A9" etc; overrides town-derived control
    ["A9"] = { enemy = false, admins = 0, troops = 0, elites = 0 },
  },
  mercs = {                              -- roster + gear; item names from weapons.json etc.
    { name = "Barry", sector = "A9", assignment = "squad", contract_days_left = 7,
      weapon = "G11", armour = "spectra", health = 100,
      items = { "MEDKIT", "CROWBAR" } },
  },
  progress = {
    quests = { HELD_IN_ALMA = "done", KINGPIN_MONEY = "in_progress" },
    facts  = { FACT_PABLO_PUNISHED_BY_PLAYER = true },
  },
  save = "my-fixture",                   -- optional: save the staged state
})
```

Semantics:

- Applied in a defined order (clock → money/difficulty → towns/sectors → roster → gear → progress) and **reconciled** afterwards, exactly as `StageBattle` reconciles sector counters: `fEnemyControlled` and the `ubNum*` / `ubNum*InBattle` counters agree, owned towns have their sectors friendly, loyalty arrays are consistent, `Team[OUR_TEAM]` matches the profiles.
- Item and skill helpers are **shared with `BattleScenario`** — extract `ItemByName`, `GiveGun`, `GiveItem`, `EquipArmour`, `ApplyStats` into one small shared unit so both harnesses use a single implementation.
- Unknown town / sector / merc / quest / fact / item names throw `std::runtime_error` with the name, like the battle harness. A spec never half-applies silently.
- Staging *replaces* the named dimensions, it does not add to them.

## Part 2 — step framework with state assertions

On top of the authoring API, build the named-milestone layer in `tests/e2e/lib/campaign.lua` (today it only has `newGame` / `hireFromAim` / `landInArulco`):

- `campaign.stage(spec)` — apply a state via `ja2.debug("campaign", spec)` and return `ja2.state()`.
- `campaign.at(spec)` — stage, then `ja2.save` + `ja2.load` so every test starts from a real save (the checkpoint helper), returning the reloaded state.
- Named-milestone assertions, e.g. `campaign.assertState{ day = 12, money = 120000, towns = { Drassen = { owned = true, loyalty = 70 } }, mercs = 4, quests = { HELD_IN_ALMA = "done" } }`.
- Read-back helpers for what the UI shows: the native map screen and laptop view models, not just globals.

## Files

- `src/game/Automation/CampaignScenario.{h,cc}` — new
- `src/game/Automation/AutomationLua.cc` — dispatch `what == "campaign"`; `GameState()` already reads money / sector / mercs
- `src/game/Automation/CMakeLists.txt`
- shared item/stat helpers (new small unit, or refactor `BattleScenario.cc`)
- `tests/e2e/lib/campaign.lua` — `stage`, `at`, `assertState` and read-back helpers
- `tests/e2e/campaign_state.lua` — new scenario
- `src/game/Automation/Automation_unittest.cc` — setter / reconciliation unit tests
- `docs/automation.md` — the new debug command
- `docs/plan/e2e-campaign-state.md` — new, short: the spec format and the save-compat contract (the plan doc for this slice)

## Definition of done

- [ ] `ja2.debug("campaign", spec)` sets day/time, money, difficulty, town ownership + loyalty + militia, sector garrisons/control, merc roster + assignments, per-merc inventory, and quest/fact progress on the live game.
- [ ] Unknown names fail with a clear message; the game does not half-apply silently.
- [ ] The staged state is save-game compatible: `campaign_state.lua` stages a non-default state, asserts `ja2.state()` and the map-screen / laptop view models, saves, reloads, and asserts again.
- [ ] `tests/e2e/lib/campaign.lua` exposes `stage` / `at` / `assertState` so a test states a milestone instead of re-implementing the setup.
- [ ] `ja2.state()` (and/or a new read surface) exposes enough to assert it: town ownership/loyalty, per-merc inventory, quest/fact state, difficulty.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the reconciliation invariants (sector counters vs `StrategicMap`, roster vs profiles, loyalty bounds).
- [ ] `./ja2 -unittests` green; the new e2e passes via `ctest -R e2e_campaign_state`.
- [ ] `docs/automation.md` documents the command; `docs/plan/e2e-campaign-state.md` records the format and contract.

## Non-goals

- **Not the rest of the campaign arc.** No hiring flow, no world-map movement steps, no long-run soak, no end-game — those stay #69–#71. This is the state-authoring + assertion foundation they build on.
- No new gameplay and no parallel state; no new save format and no byte-compatibility promise.
- Not a "replay history to any day" simulator: it sets state, it does not replay the events that led there.

## References

- Plan (tactical analogue): `docs/plan/e2e-tactical-battles.md`
- Harness to mirror: `src/game/Automation/BattleScenario.cc`, `tests/e2e/lib/battle.lua`, `tests/e2e/battle_smoke.lua`
- Save surface: `src/game/SaveLoadGame.cc` — `SaveGeneralInfo`, `SaveLaptopInfoToSavedGame`, `SaveMercProfiles`, `SaveStrategicInfoToSavedFile`, `SaveStrategicTownLoyaltyToSaveGameFile`, `SaveStrategicStatusToSaveGameFile`, `SaveSoldierStructure`
- Merged from #155 (the state-authoring slice folded into this one).

issues.body:
## Summary

Two fixed costs are paid on **every** `make` on the Windows/MSYS2 dev loop, even when nothing changed. Together they dominate a no-op build:

| step | time |
|---|---|
| no-op `make -j12` | **9.0 s** |
| of which: `cargo build` + `rustc` on `stracciatella_c_api` | **7–8 s** |
| asset `copy_directory` after each relink (`externalized/`, `unittests/`, `mods/`, `ui/`) | **~10 s** |
| touch 1 file + relink | 29.6 s |

Measured on `C:\Workspace\ja2-stracciatella\_bin` (MSYS2 MinGW64, GCC 16.1, CMake 4.3.4, 12 cores).

## 1. The Rust staticlib is rebuilt on every build

`rust/stracciatella_c_api/build.rs` prints its `rerun-if-changed` path with the `{:?}` (Debug) format, which wraps the path in literal double quotes:

```rust
println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={:?}", &header_path);
```

Cargo then looks for a file literally named `"C:/…/include/stracciatella.h"` (quotes included), never finds it, and marks the crate dirty on every invocation. Verified with `CARGO_LOG=cargo::core::compiler::fingerprint=info`:

```
stale: missing "…\stracciatella_c_api\"C:/…/lib-stracciatella/include/stracciatella.h\""
fingerprint dirty for stracciatella_c_api v0.1.0
```

Consequence: `cargo build --profile release-with-debug` re-runs `rustc` + relink of the staticlib on every single `make`, and CMake re-runs the copy steps for it.

**Fix:** print the path with `Display` instead of `Debug`:

```rust
println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", header_path.display());
```

Expected: no-op build 9 s → ~2 s.

## 2. Asset directories are fully recopied on every relink

`copy_assets_dir_to_ja2_binary_after_build()` and the `ja2-ui-assets` target use `cmake -E copy_directory`, which rewrites every file unconditionally — ~10 s of I/O after each link, even when no asset changed.

**Fix:** use `cmake -E copy_directory_if_different` (added in CMake 3.26) when the running CMake supports it, falling back to `copy_directory` on older CMake (the project's `cmake_minimum_required` is 3.18.1, and Android NDK toolchains may ship older CMake).

## Scope

- [x] Fix the `rerun-if-changed` quoting bug
- [x] Copy assets only when they differ
- [ ] (follow-up, separate) install `sccache` on dev machines, `-fuse-ld=lld`, `-G Ninja`, `CMAKE_UNITY_BUILD=ON` — larger toolchain discussion

No user-visible behaviour change: the same files end up in the same places, just without the redundant work.

## Result (merged in #82)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| no-op `make -j12` | 9.0 s | **3.1 – 4.4 s** |
| `rustc` on `stracciatella_c_api` when nothing changed | every build | **0 runs** |
| asset copies after relink | rewrites every file, ~10 s | writes nothing when unchanged |
| touch 1 file + relink | 29.6 s | **15.7 s** |
| `ja2 -unittests` | — | 224/224 pass |

**Status: delivered.** Fixed by #29 (merged `c4dc4daa7`); recorded here because #77 landed while that PR was in flight and made the issue — not a board draft item — the unit of work. The draft item that used to hold this text has been removed, so the board still tracks it exactly once.

**Labels:** `task`, `build`. **Milestone:** none — housekeeping under `Repo & CI` is not a shippable increment.

## Definition of done

- [x] The `Free Disk Space (Ubuntu)` step is gone from `github-ci.yml`. The runner shows 86 GiB free at job start and the build needs single-digit GiB; the step cost **94 s (Linux) / 102 s (mingw64)** of every job to reclaim space that is never used. It only ever existed for the Android build this fork dropped in #26.
- [x] A `concurrency` group keyed on `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress` cancels a superseded run instead of letting it burn the full 4-job matrix to completion. Per-ref grouping means different PRs, tags and master never cancel each other.
- [x] CI is green with the step removed — that run is the proof the disk was never needed.
- [x] The saving shows up in step timings, and the cancellation was exercised live.

## Evidence

`df` from the cleaner's own log, at job start:

```
before  /dev/root  151263856  61019160   90228312  41% /   ← 86 GiB available
after   /dev/root  151263856  37669756  113577716  25% /
```

Measured in the PR run vs. the master run it was compared against (full table in #29): all 4 checks pass with the step absent, step order now `Set up job → Context in env → Checkout`.

The `concurrency` proof: push 1 created run 37107762665; push 2 ~2 min later left it `cancelled` and started 37107836109 instead. Before the change, the stale run would have ground through all 4 jobs.

Cross-run *totals* swing by minutes for unrelated reasons (mingw64's sccache hit rate, `appimagelint`'s mirror fetch at 84–109 s), so the reliable number is the step-level one: 94–102 s per job of deterministic work is no longer performed.

Delivered by #29.

## What

Carry the build-toolchain findings from #78 to their conclusion: remove the remaining fixed overhead from the Windows/MSYS2 dev loop, and bring the pinned third-party versions up to date.

1. **sccache** ΓÇö install it on the dev machine (CMake already wires `CMAKE_*_COMPILER_LAUNCHER`, and Cargo already uses it as `RUSTC_WRAPPER`, so nothing in the repo is needed beyond it being on `PATH`).
2. **lld** ΓÇö link with `ld.lld` when the toolchain ships it (links of the monolithic `ja2` cost ~7.4 s with GNU ld). New `USE_LLD` option, default `ON`, GNU compilers only, silently falls back when `ld.lld` is absent.
3. **Ninja** ΓÇö verify `-G Ninja` works end to end here and document it as the recommended generator (it is installed already; MSYS Make forks a shell per recipe line).
4. **Unity builds** ΓÇö the tree carries `UNITY_GROUP` / `SKIP_UNITY_BUILD_INCLUSION` plumbing but nothing ever sets `CMAKE_UNITY_BUILD`. Verify it builds and tests clean and document how to switch it on.
5. **Dependency bumps**:
   | dep | from | to |
   |---|---|---|
   | Lua | 5.3.6 (EOL) | **5.5.1** (sol2 already carries a `lua-55.patch`) |
   | googletest | 1.16.0 | **1.18.0** |
   | magic_enum | 0.9.7 | **0.9.8** |
   | RmlUi | 6.1 | **6.3** |
   | SDL3 | 3.4.14 | **3.4.16** (vendored VC/mingw/macOS trees + source-builder URL) |

## Definition of done

- [x] `cmake` reports `Using sccache found at ΓÇª` and `Linking with lld found at ΓÇª`
- [x] a no-op build and a single-file relink are no slower than before this change
- [x] `-G Ninja` configured, built and tested from scratch, documented in `COMPILATION.md`
- [x] `-DCMAKE_UNITY_BUILD=ON` configured, built and tested, documented
- [x] all five dependency bumps land with their new pinned hashes
- [x] local validation on MSYS2 MinGW64: fresh build, `ja2 -unittests` green, e2e subset green, headless boot smoke
- [x] CI green on the PR; **No visual change**


## Result

Merged in #89 (squash `ceb2b1f73`).

| item | outcome |
|---|---|
| sccache | `Using sccache found at C:/msys64/mingw64/bin/sccache.exe` |
| lld | `Linking with lld found at .../ld.lld.exe`; new `USE_LLD` option (default ON, GNU only) |
| Ninja | full build green, **no-op 1-2 s** (MSYS Make: 3.1-4.4 s), binary passes 224/224, documented |
| Unity | build 463 s, **239 of 451 sources compile as 9 translation units**, 224/224 unit + 2/2 spike; needed one `SKIP_UNITY_BUILD_INCLUSION` (two container unittests both define a global `TestEntity`), and `make -k` over the tree showed that to be the only collision |
| dep bumps | Lua 5.5.1, googletest 1.18.0, magic_enum 0.9.8, RmlUi 6.3, SDL3 3.4.16 (vendored VC/mingw/macOS trees) |
| local validation | 224/224 unit, 9/9 spike, 2/2 e2e, headless boot to MAINMENU_SCREEN |
| CI | Linux, Linux mingw64 (links the vendored SDL3 3.4.16), lint linux, lint windows - all green |

Two build bugs were found and fixed on the way (both described in the PR): sol2 was silently half
patched because its `execute_process` result was never checked, and a bumped dependency left stale
objects linked against the new headers (`cmake/DepRefresh.cmake`).

Follow-up noted in the PR: only the nine declared `UNITY_GROUP`s are batched - the ~200 sources
without one still compile one file per translation unit.

issues.body:
## Problem

`tests/e2e/check_resolution.py::compare()` is already a tolerant ("lossy") compare — a channel counts as different only if it is off by more than `--tolerance` (default 8/255), and a shot fails only when more than `--max-diff-pct` (default 0.05%) of pixels differ. Byte-equality is only the **fast path** added in #83:

```python
if a.read_bytes() == b.read_bytes():   # same build + same encoder -> identical bytes
    w, h = png_size(a)
    return 0, w * h
```

When that fast path does **not** hold, the fallback decodes both PNGs with the pure-Python Paeth unfilter in `read_png()`. That decode, not the tolerance, is the cost — and it is enormous at widescreen sizes.

Measured here on the largest committed golden (`golden/3440x1440/mapscreen_parity/mapscreen_assignment.png`, 2.6 MB, 3440x1440 RGB):

| step | time |
|---|---|
| byte fast path (read ×2 + memcmp) | 0.021 s |
| current `read_png` decode (one image) | **10.4 s** |
| Pillow load | 0.14 s |
| Pillow + numpy load + compare | ~0.3 s |

So a *passing* run is already effectively free (no decode), but any run where the bytes differ pays ~10 s per image / ~20 s per pair. #83 documents "9.1 s on one 3440x1440 PNG (17.9 s for a whole compare)". The corpus is **191 goldens / 141 MB** (3440x1440 alone is 34 files / 42 MB), and the build-hash version line alone can force the slow path on ~15 goldens across builds.

This is the only remaining pathological path in the resolution suite. It is a developer/regeneration tool (CI runs only `ctest -L '^spike$'`), so a slow failure path is easy to hit and expensive to wait on.

## Proposal

Keep the byte-identical fast path. Replace the pure-Python decode in the fallback with a native decoder **when one is importable**, and keep the stdlib decoder as the fallback:

- Use Pillow (`PIL.Image`) for `read_png()` when available; `numpy` for the per-pixel compare loop when available.
- Keep the current stdlib implementation working unchanged when Pillow/numpy are absent — the harness must stay runnable with only the Python standard library, so this is an optional accelerator, not a new hard dependency.
- Document the optional dependency in `tests/e2e/golden/README.md`.

Do **not** rewrite this in Rust: comparison is not the bottleneck on the passing path (0.02 s/image), and a Rust test binary would add a second toolchain artifact pipeline on Windows/MSYS2 and macOS for a step that already costs seconds. Pillow decodes the same image ~74× faster than the current decoder and is already present in the local dev environment.

Optional follow-up (separate issue if wanted): stop letting the build hash in the version line force the slow path at all — normalize/omit that region at capture time, or compare a stored digest, rather than paying a decode to discover the only difference is the hash.

## Definition of done

- [ ] `compare()`'s fallback uses a native decoder when Pillow is importable, with the existing pure-Python path retained as fallback (no new hard dependency).
- [ ] The compare loop uses numpy when importable; pure-Python loop retained otherwise.
- [ ] Benchmarks recorded in the PR: per-image decode and a full `ctest -L resolution` compare run where bytes differ, before vs after.
- [ ] `ctest -L resolution -j8` still 95/95 against unchanged goldens (`git status tests/e2e/golden` empty); a run with deliberately-differing bytes reports the same pixels.
- [ ] `tests/e2e/golden/README.md` (and `check_resolution.py` docstring) mention the optional Pillow/numpy acceleration.

## Source

Follow-up to #83 (squash `28658215b`), which added the byte fast path this issue makes non-pathological. Same area label (`automation`).

issues.body:
A pull request that only moves markdown — a doc fix, an `AGENTS.md` tweak, an issue-template wording change — currently runs the whole pipeline: two build jobs (Linux, Linux mingw64) plus two lint jobs, roughly **60 runner minutes** for a change no compiler ever reads. The workflow has no notion of what a change touches; every job runs on every event.

## Definition of done

- [ ] `github-ci.yml` gains a cheap `changes` job that reports whether this run touches anything the build or the linter can actually see.
- [ ] `ci-build` (both matrix entries) and `ci-lint` (both matrix entries) `needs: changes` and are skipped when it says no.
- [ ] Skipping is **one-sided**: the filter is an exclusion list over `**`, so a path nobody thought of still runs the full pipeline. Forgetting to exclude something costs runner minutes; wrongly excluding something would hide a broken build behind a green run. Deliberately not an allowlist.
- [ ] Markdown anywhere, `docs/`, the GitHub issue templates / `CODEOWNERS` / `dependabot.yml`, `.agents/` and the root metadata files (`.editorconfig`, `.gitignore`, `.mailmap`, `contributors.txt`, the SFI licence text) skip. C++, Rust, `CMakeLists.txt`, `cmake/`, `dependencies/`, `assets/`, `android/`, `tests/`, `tools/`, `.ci/`, `.github/workflows/`, `appveyor.yml`, `min-rust-version` and `version` always run.
- [ ] Pushes are gated too: `base:` is the push `before` commit, so a push to `nightly` is measured against the previous nightly rather than against master (the default base, which would compute an empty diff and skip the nightly build). Tag pushes have no `before` commit and are never filtered out — release builds must always run.
- [ ] Pull requests keep a green check: the `changes` job reports `false` as a skipped check, not a missing one.
- [ ] Proof: the filter logic is exercised against the real path list of this repository, and the PR that delivers this changes the workflow itself, so it runs the full matrix (the gate must not swallow its own validation).

## Plan

`dorny/paths-filter` v4.0.3, pinned to its SHA like the other third-party action (`setup-sdl`). On `pull_request` it reads the changed-file list from the REST API (needs `pull-requests: read`, no checkout); on `push` it diffs with git against `event.before`, which needs a checkout but no history beyond depth 1, because the two-dot diff does not need a merge base.

issues.body:
The game ships two executables: `ja2` (the game, `src/sgp/SGP.cc`) and `ja2-launcher` (an FLTK front-end, `src/launcher/`). The launcher only edits `ja2.json` and then spawns `ja2` as a child process (`Launcher::startExecutable`, `src/launcher/Launcher.cc:422`); the game never calls it, and both use the same Rust `EngineOptions` backend.

Most of the launcher's surface is already native: the video/audio/gameplay/controls/accessibility pages of the native Options screen (`src/game/NativeUI/FrontOptions.cc`, `assets/ui/screens/options.rml`) and the legacy video screen already change and persist resolution, window mode, UI scale, world zoom, filter and FPS to `ja2.json`. The launcher is therefore mostly redundant, and its remaining features should become native so the extra binary, the FLTK dependency and the process supervisor can go away.

## What only the launcher does today

- **Game directory picker + validation** (Data/ present, 1.13 warning). Without `game_dir` the game exits with `MissingGameDir` before any UI is drawn (`SGP.cc:410`, `rust/stracciatella/src/config/engine_options.rs:147`).
- **Save-game directory picker.**
- **Game version picker** and "guess version" (`guessResourceVersion`, already reachable from C++).
- **Mod manager**: available/enabled lists, enable/disable, reorder priority, mod details (`ModManager` is already in `RustInterface`).
- **Logs viewer** for the last `ja2.log`.
- **Launching the game/editor** and reporting a non-zero child exit code.

## Done when

- A native front-end (RmlUi) can configure the game end to end: pick the JA2 game directory and save-game directory, pick the resource version (with guessing), and enable/disable/reorder mods — all persisted through `EngineOptions`/`ja2.json`.
- A config-only startup path exists: when `game_dir` is unset or invalid, `ja2` opens the native setup screen instead of exiting, and offers to relaunch once a valid config is written (mod/game-dir/version changes need a content-manager restart).
- The last `ja2.log` can be read from a native screen, and a crash still leaves an obvious path to it.
- `ja2` alone launches and plays the game with no launcher present.
- `src/launcher/` is removed, `BUILD_LAUNCHER` and FLTK are dropped from the build, and packaging/launchers point at `ja2`: `assets/distr-files-mac/ja2-startup.sh:11`, `assets/distr-files-linux/ja2-stracciatella.desktop:5`, `assets/distr-files-linux/man6/ja2.6:14`, and the CPack NSIS lines in `CMakeLists.txt:536-538`.
- Unit tests, `ctest -L e2e` and `ctest -L resolution` are green.
- Screenshot proof on the `pr-screenshots` branch at 640x480 and 1920x1080 (plus 2560x1080 or 3440x1440 if the layout depends on width), with a caption per screen; the setup screen, the mods screen and the logs screen each get goldens.

## Notes

- The settings backend already exists (`GCM->saveVideoSettings`, `saveNativeUiSettings`, `EngineOptions_write`); no new persistence layer is needed.
- The native UI is configured right after `EngineOptions_create`, before game data loads, so a setup screen can render when `loadGameData` would fail.
- Losing the launcher loses the parent process that catches crashes and shows logs; the replacement needs an in-process crash path or the log screen must be reachable on the next start.
- Plan: `docs/plan/native-modern-game.md`. This work is best split into sub-issues (setup screen, mods screen, version picker, logs, packaging) when it starts.

issues.body:
## Context
1.13's defining feature. Weapons become platforms and gear becomes a loadout. This is the single biggest feel upgrade of the revamp, and the schema other tactical systems (ammo, condition, content) hang off.

## Design principles applied
- Revamp is default: NAS replaces the vanilla attachment slots outright, no legacy mode.
- Native-first: inventory/attachment rules are engine C++ structs and functions, not runtime JSON. Leaf tunables (slot counts, compatibility strictness) are toggles.
- Testable by construction: rules are pure enough to unit-test, and loadouts are drivable headless.

## Native shape
- Inventory/attachment model as engine types + rule functions.
- UI redrawn in the native layer (view model over the new toolkit), not the old 640x480 HUD.

## Test surface
- Unit tests for slot and compatibility rules.
- e2e loadout -> combat scenarios driven by ja2ctl.

## Open questions for the brainstorm
- Slot model: how close to NAS 2.0? Which body locations? How deep does LBE nesting go?
- How the native UI presents a deep loadout without overwhelming a 16:9 screen.
- Migration of existing saves/content is explicitly not a constraint (revamp is default).


## Equipment revamp: detail and dependencies
**Proposed (owner decides):** typed slots (optic, muzzle, underbarrel, side rail, magazine well), 3 to 5 per weapon class; compatibility by mount type, never a per-weapon whitelist; about 15 to 20 attachments total, each with one real trade-off. LBE = vest, belt, pack with typed pockets; nesting depth one; weight feeds #140.
**Depends on:** nothing; this is the schema root. **Unblocks:** #97, #98, #100, #101, #260, #261, #262, #263.
**Definition of done:** engine item/slot/pocket types; compatibility and pocket-fit rules; unit tests for both; a loadout buildable headless (#263).

---

## Definition of done
- `Brain` interface: `decide(briefing) -> [tool calls]`, with the LLM implementation (and the test-only scripted/replay implementation from the decision log issue).
- Agent loop: assemble briefing -> LLM call with tool schemas -> validate and schedule tool calls -> feed errors and order results back; per-turn call budget; illegal calls return errors she can retry.
- Adaptive cadence: daily while she is unaware or preoccupied, tighter as alarm rises; early-wake triggers for urgent events.
- Persona prompt (lore, temperament from #115, her scratchpad / diary carried in the save).
- Provider abstraction (Anthropic first, OpenAI-compatible endpoint as a stretch) using the settings from the settings page issue.
- Applies the policy from the "decision: strategic clock policy" issue.
- The LLM output is only tool calls; it never writes game state. Player free text reaches her only as bounded intents (see #118).

Tool API and executor, Belief store and briefing builder, LLM provider settings page.

## Test surface

- Bounded player verbs mapped to native intents: negotiate, provoke, propaganda, ransom, prisoner exchange, psyops, and deception (decoy squads, false radio traffic, feints).

- She can bluff and weigh offers against her real position; outcomes resolve natively from belief, resources and temperament.
- Player free text is parsed to the bounded intent set natively and never inserted raw into her prompt.
- Communicated to the player through tells and her replies so it feels fair.

issues.body:
The `Linux mingw64` job never hits the compiler cache: it recompiles all of its ~650 C++ translation units on every run, which makes it the longest job in the matrix (~11 min, while the native `Linux` job is ~9 min **and** runs the whole test suite).

## Root cause

- CMake's `Windows-GNU` platform module sets `CMAKE_<LANG>_USE_RESPONSE_FILE_FOR_INCLUDES=1`, so a Windows-target build passes include paths in a GCC argument file (`@file`).
- `.ci/ci-functions.sh` pins **sccache v0.5.4**, which refuses to cache *any* GCC `@file` invocation (`CompilerArguments::CannotCache("@", None)`). Modern sccache expands the response file before hashing.
- Result: every C++ compile on the mingw64 job bypasses the cache.

Evidence from [run 37122594871 / job 111201564427](https://github.com/adhikasp/ja2-stracciatella/actions/runs/37122594871/job/111201564427):

| sccache | Linux mingw64 | Linux (native) |
|---|---|---|
| C/C++ cache hits | 32 | 652 |
| Cache misses | 0 | 39 |
| Non-cacheable calls | 756 (701 reason `@`) | 58 (no `@`) |

## Definition of done

- sccache bumped to a release that expands response files before hashing (**v0.18.0**); verified locally that an `@rsp` compile is a miss when cold and a hit when warm.
- The `-sccache-vN` cache key bumped to `v2`, so a run never restores a cache written by the old binary.
- On a warm `Linux mingw64` run the job reports C/C++ cache hits, no `@` non-cacheable reason, and runs measurably faster than the ~11 min baseline.

No visual change.
issues.title: ci: make the mingw64 C++ build cacheable (sccache @file fix)

issues.body:
The repository's GitHub Actions cache is **over the 10 GB budget (10.68 GB)** and most of it can never produce a hit.

Measured on 2026-10-03 (`gh api repos/adhikasp/ja2-stracciatella/actions/caches`):

- 38 entries, 10.68 GB total.
- 33 of them are sccache, 7.76 GB.
- Entries are dominated by `linux-sccache-v1-refs/pull/<N>/merge-<sha>` — caches written by pull requests.

A cache written by a pull request is scoped to that PR's merge ref, so no other run — not `master`, not another PR, not a later run of the same PR after a rebase — can restore it. Every push therefore uploads a fresh few-hundred-MB cache that is pure waste, and it accelerates eviction of the `refs/heads/master` cache every run actually restores from.

## Definition of done

- The build job **restores** the sccache and Rust caches on every run, and **saves** them only when `github.ref` is the repository's default branch.
- The Rust save is skipped when the content-addressed key already matched exactly (avoids redundant re-uploads; the key is `hashFiles('rust')`-based).
- Pull-request runs still get cache hits, because they restore the default branch's seed and only rebuild what changed.
- No visual change.

Follow-up to #148 (the sccache upgrade, which makes the mingw64 job cacheable in the first place).
issues.title: ci: stop writing per-PR Actions caches (save only from the default branch)

## Problem

The tactical track got a harness — `BattleScenario.cc`, `ja2.debug("battle", spec)` — that stages an arbitrary fight. The strategic layer has nothing equivalent. An e2e test can only reach a campaign state by *playing* the default campaign through the UI (`lib/campaign.lua`: `newGame` → `hireFromAim` → `landInArulco`) or by loading a save someone built earlier (`lib/mapcampaign.lua`). Neither lets a test **state** the campaign it needs — "day 12, Drassen + Alma held at 70 % loyalty, 120k funds, four mercs with custom gear, `HELD_IN_ALMA` done".

We want to define that state directly, and — critically — have it be a **real, save-game-compatible state**: the same globals the game serialises, so `ja2.save()` then `ja2.load()` round-trips and the result is indistinguishable from a state reached by play.

## Save-compatibility contract

The harness mutates the live campaign globals that `SaveLoadGame.cc` writes. No parallel/duplicate state, no new save format, no fixture blob:

| State | Globals | Serialised by |
|---|---|---|
| money | `LaptopSaveInfo.iCurrentBalance` | `SaveLaptopInfoToSavedGame` |
| day / time | `guiDay`, `guiHour`, `guiMin` (world clock) | `SaveGeneralInfo` / clock |
| difficulty | `gGameOptions.ubDifficultyLevel` (1..3) | game options |
| sector control / garrison | `StrategicMap[].fEnemyControlled`, `SectorInfo[].ubNumAdmins/Troops/Elites` (+ `*InBattle`) | `SaveStrategicInfoToSavedFile`, `LoadSaveSectorInfo` |
| town loyalty / militia | `gTownLoyalty[].ubRating/fStarted`, `SectorInfo[].ubNumberOfCivsAtLevel[]`, `gfTownUsesLoyalty` | `SaveStrategicTownLoyaltyToSaveGameFile` |
| merc roster | `gMercProfiles[].bMercStatus/sSector/bAssignment`, team list (`HireMerc`, `AddSoldierToTeamAndMinimap`) | `SaveMercProfiles`, `SaveSoldierStructure` |
| per-merc inventory | `SOLDIERTYPE.inv[]` (`CreateItems` / `AutoPlaceObject`) | `SaveSoldierStructure` |
| progress | `gubQuest[]`, `gubFact[]` (`SetFactTrue`, `SetQuest`) | `SaveStrategicStatusToSaveGameFile` |

The test that proves the contract: stage → `ja2.save("fixture")` → `ja2.load("fixture")` → `ja2.state()` / view models unchanged.

## API (baked into this task)

New `src/game/Automation/CampaignScenario.{h,cc}`, wired as `ja2.debug("campaign", spec)` — same shape and conventions as `BattleScenario`. Spec:

```lua
ja2.debug("campaign", {
  day = 12, hour = 9, minute = 0,       -- world clock
  money = 120000,
  difficulty = 2,                        -- 1..3
  towns = {                              -- keyed by town id or name
    ["Drassen"] = { owned = true, loyalty = 70, militia = { green = 5, regular = 3, elite = 1 } },
  },
  sectors = {                            -- "A9" etc; overrides town-derived control
    ["A9"] = { enemy = false, admins = 0, troops = 0, elites = 0 },
  },
  mercs = {                              -- roster + gear; item names from weapons.json etc.
    { name = "Barry", sector = "A9", assignment = "squad", contract_days_left = 7,
      weapon = "G11", armour = "spectra", health = 100,
      items = { "MEDKIT", "CROWBAR" } },
  },
  progress = {
    quests = { HELD_IN_ALMA = "done", KINGPIN_MONEY = "in_progress" },
    facts  = { FACT_PABLO_PUNISHED_BY_PLAYER = true },
  },
  save = "my-fixture",                   -- optional: save the staged state
})
```

Semantics:

- Applied in a defined order (clock → money/difficulty → towns/sectors → roster → gear → progress) and **reconciled** afterwards, exactly as `StageBattle` reconciles sector counters: `fEnemyControlled` and the `ubNum*` / `ubNum*InBattle` counters agree, owned towns have their sectors friendly, loyalty arrays are consistent, `Team[OUR_TEAM]` matches the profiles.
- Item and skill helpers are **shared with `BattleScenario`** — extract `ItemByName`, `GiveGun`, `GiveItem`, `EquipArmour`, `ApplyStats` into one small shared unit so both harnesses use a single implementation.
- Unknown town / sector / merc / quest / fact / item names throw `std::runtime_error` with the name, like the battle harness. A spec never half-applies silently.
- Staging *replaces* the named dimensions, it does not add to them.

## Files

- `src/game/Automation/CampaignScenario.{h,cc}` — new
- `src/game/Automation/AutomationLua.cc` — dispatch `what == "campaign"`; `GameState()` already reads money / sector / mercs
- `src/game/Automation/CMakeLists.txt`
- shared item/stat helpers (new small unit, or refactor `BattleScenario.cc`)
- `tests/e2e/lib/campaign.lua` — `campaign.stage(spec)`, `campaign.at(spec)` (stage → save → reload) and small read-back helpers
- `tests/e2e/campaign_state.lua` — new scenario
- `src/game/Automation/Automation_unittest.cc` — setter / reconciliation unit tests
- `docs/automation.md` — the new debug command
- `docs/plan/e2e-campaign-state.md` — new, short: the spec format and the save-compat contract (this is the plan doc for this slice)

## Definition of done

- [ ] `ja2.debug("campaign", spec)` sets day/time, money, difficulty, town ownership + loyalty + militia, sector garrisons/control, merc roster + assignments, per-merc inventory, and quest/fact progress on the live game.
- [ ] Unknown names fail with a clear message; the game does not half-apply silently.
- [ ] The staged state is save-game compatible: `campaign_state.lua` stages a non-default state, asserts `ja2.state()` and the map-screen / laptop view models, saves, reloads, and asserts again.
- [ ] `ja2.state()` (and/or a new read surface) exposes enough to assert it: town ownership/loyalty, per-merc inventory, quest/fact state, difficulty.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the reconciliation invariants (sector counters vs `StrategicMap`, roster vs profiles, loyalty bounds).
- [ ] `./ja2 -unittests` green; the new e2e passes via `ctest -R e2e_campaign_state`.
- [ ] `docs/automation.md` documents the command; `docs/plan/e2e-campaign-state.md` records the format and contract.

## Non-goals

- **Not the campaign arc.** No hiring flow, no world-map steps, no soak, no end-game — those stay #68–#71. This is only the state-authoring layer they build on.
- No new gameplay and no parallel state; no new save format and no byte-compatibility promise.
- Not a "replay history to any day" simulator: it sets state, it does not replay the events that led there.

## References

- Plan (tactical analogue): `docs/plan/e2e-tactical-battles.md`
- Harness to mirror: `src/game/Automation/BattleScenario.cc`, `tests/e2e/lib/battle.lua`, `tests/e2e/battle_smoke.lua`
- Consumers: #68 (step framework + assertions), #66 (goal), #67 (campaign plan doc)
- Save surface: `src/game/SaveLoadGame.cc` — `SaveGeneralInfo`, `SaveLaptopInfoToSavedGame`, `SaveMercProfiles`, `SaveStrategicInfoToSavedFile`, `SaveStrategicTownLoyaltyToSaveGameFile`, `SaveStrategicStatusToSaveGameFile`, `SaveSoldierStructure`

issues.body:
## What

A headless sector transition burns **~85–97 s** at native resolutions (`>=1280x720`), and it dominates every battle/campaign e2e scenario. At 640x480 the same transition is ~0.8 s.

`BeginLoadScreen()` (`src/game/Strategic/StrategicMap.cc:197`) busy-waits a 2 s *virtual* fade animation: per iteration it does a full-screen `ShadowRectUsingLowPercentTable` + `BltStretchVideoSurface` and calls `RefreshScreen()`. In headless automation this loop advances the virtual clock through the slow clock-read fallback rather than a normal present, so it takes far more (and far more expensive) iterations than the 2 s of game time it represents. Once the native UI is active (`>=1280x720`) each iteration is much heavier, so the cost explodes with resolution.

## Measurements (Ryzen 5 5560U, build 32d95ce63, headless)

| Scenario | Total | Inside the sector load | Frames stepped |
|---|---|---|---|
| `battle_campaign.lua` @1920x1080 | 100.3 s | **~79–90 s** in `campaign.enterTown()` (one load) | 199 |
| `battle_smoke.lua` @1920x1080 | 113.5 s | **~97 s** in `campaign.startWithTeam()` (Omerta landing) | ~11 200 |
| same sector load @640x480 | — | **~0.8 s** | — |

- `battle_smoke`'s actual combat is only ~15 s (5 turns); ~86 % of its wall time is the landing.
- `-frame-ms 100` / `-frame-ms 5000` do **not** shorten it — the loop's time advance is independent of the frame quantum.
- This is why the resolution matrix at 1920+ is hours long (historical `resolution_mapscreen_equivalence_3440x1440` = 667 s, `resolution_mapscreen_parity_1920x1080` = 961 s) — those tours run many sector transitions.

## Definition of done

- A sector load in headless automation no longer does per-iteration full-screen software work, and/or the fade is skipped/short-circuited when nothing is going to read the frame (automation composes the frame lazily). The loading screen itself must still exist for `loadingscreen_parity.lua`.
- `ctest -R e2e_battle` drops from ~220 s to a few seconds; `e2e_battle_campaign` and `e2e_battle_smoke` still pass.
- `check_determinism.py` stays green (same seed => same frames).
- A unit test or timing guard on the loop keeps the cost from creeping back.

## Evidence

The 35-scenario profiling pass run for this issue (`ctest -L e2e` equivalent) — see the parent issue / milestone #18. Phase log shows the gap sits entirely in one call with no intermediate logging.
issues.title: bug: Headless sector-load fade costs ~85-97 s at 1280x720+ and dominates battle/campaign e2e

## What

The Windows dev build directory (`_bin`) uses the **MSYS Makefiles** generator — the docs' own "slow choice on Windows" (`COMPILATION.md#faster-builds`). Ninja is installed (`C:\msys64\mingw64\bin\ninja.exe`) but unused. sccache and lld are already on and working.

Measurements on the existing `_bin` (RelWithDebInfo, sccache + lld, parallel 6):

| Step | Time |
|---|---|
| no-op `cmake --build` | 5.1 s |
| one gameplay `.cc` content edit + link (`Weapons.cc`) | **25.9 s** |
| a 30-dependent-TU header edit + link (`Points.h`) | **89.9 s** |
| revert the same header (sccache hits) | 21.3 s |
| relink only (lld, 589 MB binary) | ~3.5 s |
| cargo up-to-date check | 1.8 s |

Per-TU compile is ~18 s, so a header-touching change costs roughly `3 s x (dependent TUs)` at 6-way. Ninja avoids a shell per recipe line and schedules better.

- A fresh build dir configured with `-G Ninja` builds the same binary and `ctest -L e2e` passes.
- Before/after numbers recorded in `COMPILATION.md#faster-builds`.
- `AGENTS.md`'s Windows daily-build block points at the generator choice and the numbers.
- A short "fast edit -> rebuild -> run" recipe for mechanic changes (which tests to run) is documented.

A build directory keeps its generator, so this needs a *fresh* `_bin` (or a sibling like `_bin_ninja`) — not a reconfigure of the current one.

## Decision

`.ci/ci-build.sh` runs only `cargo-test`, `ja2 -unittests` and `ctest -L '^spike$'`. The e2e suite (`ctest -L e2e`) and the resolution matrix **never run in CI**, so a mechanics regression that only the e2e catches is invisible to a PR — the e2e is a local-only safety net.

The blocker is game data: e2e drives the real game and needs the original JA2 Gold data (`game_dir`), which `.ci/ci-setup.sh` neither fetches nor can legally ship.

Options to weigh:

1. **Self-hosted runner** that has the game data (owner's machine / a dedicated box) runs `ctest -L e2e` on demand or nightly.
2. **A small, legally-clean fixture pack** that exercises the mechanics paths without the full data (large effort; may not reach the screens the e2e does).
3. **Keep e2e local** and instead make the local loop fast enough (the other milestone #18 issues), with CI running only the data-free spikes.

## Definition of done

- One option chosen and recorded here, with reasoning and the constraints (game data, runner cost, secrets).
- If a runner option is chosen, a follow-up task wires the job and the CTest label it runs.

## Related

- #65 (battle scenario corpus in CI) depends on this answer.
- Milestone #18 (CI & Build tooling).

issues.body:
## Goal

**The Queen is an AI agent, not a script.** An LLM is her brain. She acts on the strategic game world through a bounded set of tools, under the same kinds of constraints the player has (money, manpower, equipment, time, information), and the player should feel they are playing a "multiplayer" game against another human-like actor: same resource management and restrictions, asymmetric in the actions available and in point of view.

This issue is the design for the whole milestone. It replaces the old shape (native drives + utility policy, LLM only as voice and intent parser). Child issues are listed at the bottom.

## Decisions (made with the owner)

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Is the LLM required? | **Yes.** Without a configured LLM the game cannot start a campaign. There is no shipped "dumb Queen" fallback. |
| Who pays? | The **player's own API key**, entered on a settings page. |
| Can she beat a careless player? | **Yes.** Her resource pool is tuned later; the design must let her win. |
| One mind or a court? | **Single mind.** The court, the field officers and the fog of war are simulated by ordinary **state-machine actors** in native code, not by more LLM calls. |
| Tests and automation | A **scripted / replay Brain** exists for e2e and ja2ctl only. It is a test harness, not a gameplay mode and not a fallback. |

## Principles

1. **She is an agent with tools; the engine is her hands, eyes and rulebook.** Same model as a coding agent: she calls typed tools, the engine validates, charges, executes and returns a result or an error ("denied: insufficient funds"). She cannot do anything the rules do not offer her. The LLM never writes game state directly; it only calls tools.
2. **She sees a briefing, never the truth.** Her prompt is built natively from what her organization actually knows. Fog of war applies to her exactly as to the player.
3. **She has her own resources and her own limits.** Money, manpower, equipment stockpile, political capital, and a scarce resource of her own: attention.
4. **She has a life.** The player is not the only thing on her mind. Dealing with the player starts as a minor item on her docket and grows as the player earns it.
5. **She adapts, imperfectly.** She builds a theory of the player from what she knows, and the theory can be wrong.
6. **Native-first and testable.** All rules, costs, delays, fog and resolution are C++ with unit tests. Every LLM decision is logged and replayable, so e2e is deterministic with no network.

## 1. The agent loop

- **Turn:** a strategic window assembles a **briefing**, calls the LLM, receives zero or more **tool calls**, the engine validates and schedules them, results come back as the next briefing's "what happened to your orders".
- **Adaptive cadence:** while she is unaware or preoccupied, one turn per game day (cheap). As alarm rises it tightens to several per day, and during an active offensive to hourly. Cost scales with threat, not with playtime.
- **Triggers:** specific events can wake her early (a capital-adjacent sector lost, an officer killed, a messenger with the "urgent" flag).
- **Continuity:** she has a persistent **scratchpad / diary** tool: her theory of the enemy, standing plans, grudges, and what she is doing with her day. It is carried in the save and fed back each turn.
- **Errors are feedback:** an illegal tool call returns an error and she may retry within the turn. A per-turn call budget stops loops.

## 2. Fog of war: her belief state

Her briefing is generated natively from a **belief store**, not from game truth.

- **Sources:** garrison reports, survivors, patrol sightings, radio intercepts, informants, townsfolk rumor, later spies and recon.
- **Every report has latency, fidelity and bias.** Drassen is far from the capital, so news is a day or more old. A frightened garrison commander reports "hundreds of attackers". A corrupt one hides that the mine income stopped because he is skimming. The provincial bureaucracy filters bad news upward.
- **Distortion is native and seeded:** a deterministic function of the true event, the reporting officer's traits (cowardly, careerist, corrupt, competent, loyal) and a seeded roll. Same save, same lies.
- **Claims with confidence:** the belief store holds claims like "Drassen: local militia revolt, confidence 0.4, source Capt. Vargas, age 2 days". Later contradictory evidence updates them. The moment she realizes "this is organized, professional and led by one person" is a visible story beat.
- **Player counter-play falls out of this:** kill the messengers, cut the radio, leave no survivors, plant false trails, make an invasion look like unrest.

## 3. Court and field: state-machine actors

The court and the field are simulated by deterministic state machines. They are what turn truth into reports and her orders into reality.

- **Officers** (garrison commanders, regional governors, quartermaster, spymaster, a general): traits, loyalty, fear, corruption, competence, location, rank. They produce reports (with distortion) and carry out orders (with delay and slippage).
- **Field:** the existing strategic AI machinery (garrisons, patrols, groups, reinforcement requests) becomes the **executor**. She does not pick tiles or squads; she says "hold Drassen with 8 regulars" and the executor makes it happen.
- **Court:** factions and ministers that supply news, pressure and distractions (see "She has a life").

## 4. Resources (asymmetric but real)

| Pool | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Treasury** | Liquid cash from mine income and taxes. Losing the mines cuts it, but she learns that late. |
| **Hidden assets** | Jewelry, Swiss account, crown estates. Liquidating costs time and political capital, and each tranche is a visible escalation. |
| **Manpower** | The existing reinforcement pool, split by tier: admin, regular, elite. Elites cost money and training time. |
| **Materiel stockpile** | Guns, ammo, armor, NVGs, flares, vehicles as real stock with real deliveries and real shortages. |
| **Attention** | A scarce budget of how much she can personally deal with per day (see section 6). |
| **Political capital** | Generals, the court, foreign backers. Visible failure and overreach erode it; at the extreme it feeds coup, ceasefire or abdication arcs. |

The player sees about as much of this as they would of a human opponent's: almost nothing at first, glimpses through intel ("convoy of crates arriving in Meduna", "she is selling the crown jewels").

## 5. Her tools (action space)

Every tool has a **cost, a delay and a visibility** (what the player can detect and how). All are validated natively.

- **Force:** reinforce or reduce garrisons, set patrol levels, launch a counterattack, recall a force, set a night guard, hunter-killer teams.
- **Procurement:** hire a tier, buy an equipment class, build stock, liquidate an asset tranche, issue equipment to garrisons.
- **Intel:** order an investigation, plant informants, set a bounty, interrogate a prisoner, ask for a report from a region.
- **Political:** edicts (curfew, martial law), reprisals against a town, propaganda, bribe, negotiate, sue for peace.
- **Self:** scratchpad write, take or dismiss an audience, delegate.

## 6. She has a life: preoccupation and attention

Reacting to the player must not be the only thing the LLM does. At the start she is enjoying herself in the capital and the war barely reaches her desk.

- **The docket.** Every turn a native system builds her docket: a ranked list of things competing for her attention. Two families:
  - **Preoccupations** (the time sink): court life and personal projects drawn from a curated **event deck** with weights and schedules. Examples: a state banquet, a rivalry between generals, a foreign envoy and a trade deal, palace works, a feud over succession, a health scare, her private research. Lore details can be expanded later; the mechanism ships first.
  - **Field reports**, scored by severity x credibility x rank of the reporting officer x freshness.
- **Attention budget.** She can only deal with so much per day. Preoccupations consume it. Field reports beyond her budget sit in an **unread pile** and age, which is itself a source of delayed awareness.
- **Salience grows with the player.** A hidden **alarm** level rises as credible reports accumulate (mine lost, officer killed, an organized pattern recognized). Alarm increases her attention budget, raises the weight of war items and starts pre-empting the deck. This is the arc from "who cares, a local revolt" to "everything else can wait".
- **Her diary is part of the log.** Early in a campaign her event log and diary are mostly court life; the player occasionally appears in it. Later the log is mostly the war.
- **Tone follows state.** Drives (fear, anger, arrogance, desperation, boredom) are updated natively from events and shape the persona prompt, so her voice and her risk appetite shift with how things go.
- **Cost benefit:** while quiet, her turns are cheap, daily and mostly flavor.

## 7. Adapting to the player without reading minds

- **Native profiling** extracts features from what she *knows*, not from what the player actually did: share of night fights, simultaneous squads, stealth versus loud, weapon preferences, sector preferences, speed of expansion. These reach her as analyst notes with a confidence.
- **She chooses the doctrine.** Night ops: bigger night guard, light sticks, then NVGs when she can afford them. Many squads: quantity over quality to cover the map. Snipers: counter-snipers and cover denial. Stealth and covert: informants, checkpoints.
- **Imperfection by design:** personality, memory, delay and wrong theories. She counters what she believes is happening, which the player can exploit with feints and deception.

## 8. Escalation and lore

Escalation unlocks on **her belief about the threat**, not on the player's progress percentage.

- **Phase 0, unrest:** local garrisons only, no liquidation, court life dominates.
- **Phase 1, organized hostile:** regulars are sent, funds start being raised.
- **Phase 2, mine income lost:** the hidden-asset ladder opens, elites become hirable.
- **Phase 3, existential:** martial law, reserves committed, negotiation and desperation options appear.

Difficulty becomes **resources + information quality + her competence**, not hidden stat cheats.

## 9. Player interaction as information warfare

The old verbs (negotiate, provoke, propaganda, ransom, prisoner exchange, psyops) become **inputs to her information channel**. Deception is the best new gameplay: decoy squads, false radio traffic, loud diversions while the real team goes quietly. Negotiation weighs her real position, and she can bluff. Free text from the player is mapped to a bounded intent set natively; it never reaches her prompt raw.

## 10. Readability: tells and the Queen's file

- **Tells:** intercepted orders, edicts, rumors in towns, radio chatter, visible deliveries, her taunts.
- **The Queen's file:** a post-hoc view of what she believed against what was true, her diary and her decisions. It is the payoff for the player and the debug tool for us.

## 11. Architecture and constraints

- **Brain interface:** `decide(briefing) -> [tool calls]`. Implementations: the LLM Brain (shipped) and a scripted/replay Brain (tests only).
- **Provider:** a settings page in the native UI takes an API key, provider and model, with a cost cap. Starting a campaign without a working configuration is blocked with a clear message.
- **Determinism:** every briefing, tool call and result is logged in the save. Replay uses the log, so e2e and regression runs reproduce exactly with no network.
- **Failure policy (decision pending):** what happens to the strategic clock when the LLM is slow, rate limited or offline. See the decision issue below.
- **Safety:** the prompt contains only the briefing and her persona; player text is never inserted unbounded; the LLM output is only tool calls that the engine validates.
- **Save format:** no compatibility obligations (see AGENTS.md).

## 12. Strategic AI levers, events and capabilities this needs

The existing strategic layer (`Strategic_AI.cc`: garrisons, patrols, reinforcement pool and points, attack groups) is a good executor but exposes too few levers and too few events. New mechanics, each its own child issue:

- **Strategic event bus and ground-truth facts API**: typed events (sector lost, mine captured, officer killed, convoy ambushed, prisoner taken, radio jammed...) that officers, the belief store and the profiler all consume.
- **Communications network**: radio, couriers, relays and jamming; the infrastructure behind latency and fog.
- **Logistics**: depots, convoys and supply lines the player can interdict.
- **Garrison levers**: tier mix, night shifts, equipment issue per garrison (ties to the equipment-aware loadouts work).
- **Operations levers**: counterattack, hunter-killer teams, sabotage of player mines, assassination squads (extends the operational layer of the AI enhancement track).
- **Occupation levers**: edicts, curfews, reprisals, bounties, informants (ties to town loyalty and the deed ledger).
- **Resource model**: treasury, hidden assets, manpower tiers, stockpile, political capital.
- **Tool API and executor**: the typed action surface with cost, delay and visibility.

## Open questions

- Which provider(s) at launch (Anthropic first? OpenAI-compatible endpoint for local models?), and the default model.
- Latency and failure policy (decision issue).
- Content depth of the preoccupation deck and the lore for the capital court (can expand later).
- How to reconcile with the existing AGENTS.md principle text ("optional LLM layer", "deterministic stub"); it needs a follow-up edit once this design is accepted.
- Exposure of the Queen's file: always on, or earned through intel?

## Definition of done for the milestone

A new campaign requires a configured LLM. The Queen starts unaware and occupied. As the player acts, her belief state, attention and doctrine change visibly. She spends her own resources, makes mistakes from bad information, adapts to the player's style, and is able to beat a careless player. Every decision is logged and replayable, and e2e arcs (unaware to alarmed, escalation, negotiated peace) run headless on the scripted Brain.

## Child issues

**Foundations (strategic mechanics and fog)**
- [ ] #180 Strategic event bus and ground-truth facts API
- [ ] #182 Court and field actors (officer state machines)
- [ ] #183 Communications network (radio, couriers, jamming)
- [ ] #181 Belief store and briefing builder
- [ ] #184 Resource model

**Her mind**
- [ ] #185 Tool API and executor over the strategic AI
- [ ] #115 Temperament (drive state)
- [ ] #186 Preoccupations and the attention docket (her life)
- [ ] #117 Brain interface, agent loop and LLM integration
- [ ] #187 LLM provider settings page and start-campaign gate
- [ ] #189 decision: strategic clock policy when the LLM is slow or offline
- [ ] #188 Decision log, replay and scripted Brain (tests only)

**New strategic levers**
- [ ] #193 Garrison levers
- [ ] #194 Operations levers
- [ ] #195 Occupation levers
- [ ] #192 Logistics
- [ ] #190 Player profiler and doctrine
- [ ] #191 Escalation phases, liquidation ladder and lore

**Player-facing**
- [ ] #118 Player interaction as information warfare
- [ ] #196 The Queen's file and tells

**Proof**
- [ ] #197 E2E arcs on the scripted Brain

Closed as superseded: #116 (utility policy).

Suggested order: #180 -> #182 / #183 -> #181 -> #184 -> #185 -> #188 -> #117 + #187 (+ decide #189) -> #186 / #115 -> levers (#193, #194, #195, #192) -> #190 / #191 -> #118 / #196 -> #197. The foundations and the scripted Brain come first so every later piece is testable before any real LLM call.

Related, outside this milestone: #54 (AI enhancement), #142 (strategic AI operational layer), #108 (equipment-aware loadouts), #113 (deed ledger), #144 (town loyalty), #133 (covert ops), #139 (prisoners).

## Context
**Placeholder / canary.** An idea we have claimed but not planned. Do not start the full build before this is scoped; the canary slice below is the proof the idea works.

The Queen's faction gets a **cast**: authored, named people (commanders, lieutenants, later more) who are real actors in the world and, at the same time, the sensors and hands of the Queen's mind. The abstract officer state machines live in the Queen's Mind milestone (#182); this issue is their **embodiment**: names, faces, placement, persistence, tactical identity. One shared record, two views: a mind-side officer and a body-side NPC.

Part of the goal #179 (Queen's Mind) from the people side.

## The idea
- **Tiers:** court (general, spymaster, quartermaster), regional governor, garrison commander, field lieutenant, sergeant. **v1 starts at garrison commander and lieutenant.**
- **Authored only.** No procedural promotion for now. The roster is large and pre-seeded across regions, so the player meets them often.
- **Encounter density (targets, tunable):** a named Queen-faction person in roughly 1-2 of every 3-4 random encounters, and almost always at points of interest: cities, mines, SAM sites, depots, checkpoints.
- **Hostile by default and fight to the end.** They can be wounded, flee, be captured, or be killed. Killed means killed; no plot armor.
- **Curated exceptions:** a handful of named commanders carry authored defection or turning events and quests. These are tied to the intel mechanic (see the intel canary issue).
- **Off-screen state machine:** posting, rotation, promotion and demotion after failure, wounded, fled, captured, dead, vacancy chain. Corruption and ambition feed the distortion of the Queen's reports (#182). Unpaid garrisons desert when her income collapses (resource model, #184).
- **Vacancy chain:** a dead commander leaves a vacancy. The Queen learns late (fog). A replacement arrives days later with different traits.
- **A fleeing survivor is an information leak:** what he saw (the player's gear, habits, squad shape) travels up the chain into her belief store and the player profiler (#190). Killing the fleeing has a reputation cost if they were surrendering (#113).
- **Documents and uniforms** on officers: rosters, orders and code books as intel items and tells (#196).
- **Tactical identity:** a named enemy is a real soldier with a persistent profile, rank-scaled stats, personal morale and temperament, and memory of the player (barks and taunts).
- **Dossier:** the player's mirror of the Queen's file. They know her people only as far as their intel reaches.

## Canary slice (definition of done)
Three authored garrison commanders (Drassen plus two more towns), each with traits, a status state machine and a vacancy chain, placed in the world and encounterable.
- Kill the Drassen commander: a vacancy opens, the Queen's briefing shows a reporting gap, and a replacement with different traits arrives after a delay.
- Runs headless and asserted in e2e on the scripted Brain.
- Unit tests on the status machine and the vacancy chain.
- Registers in the native people content registry from #156 (new NpcKind for Queen-faction people), with a test that every authored person is accounted for.

## Curation rules
- Every named role must change something in a system (reports, doctrine, vacancy, quests, intel). No name without a mechanic.
- Authored roster targets and encounter-density targets are tunables, tuned after the canary.

## Depends on
- #182 Court and field actors (mind-side officers)
- #180 Strategic event bus
- #156 People content registry (done)

## Related

- #119 Citizens who remember, #109 World texture (defection, black market)
- #139 Prisoners (capture, interrogation), #133 Covert ops (disguise)
- #110 Content: curated mercs, NPCs and quests, #111 voices and faces, #112 maps and sectors
- #113 Deed ledger, #108 Tactical AI: equipment-aware loadouts
- Intel canary: #201

## Open questions
- Size and distribution of the authored roster per region.
- Faces, voices and names pipeline (#111).
- How lieutenants attach to groups and patrols in the strategic AI (#142).

## Context
**Placeholder / canary.** An idea we have claimed but not planned. A whole mechanic branch about **intel** is expected later; this issue holds its place and defines the smallest slice that proves it.

Intel is the player's side of the fog of war. The Queen sees the world through officers' reports (Queen's Mind milestone, #181 and #182). The player knows her organization only as far as their intel reaches. That makes the fog symmetric: she has a file on the player, the player has a dossier on her.

## The idea
- **Sources of intel:** interrogated prisoners (#139), documents and uniforms taken from officers, intercepted radio and couriers (#183), informants in towns, townsfolk rumor (#109), scouting and recon, and bribed or turned officers.
- **What intel reveals:** names, ranks, traits and postings of her people, garrison composition and shifts, supply routes and depots, her orders and tells, and which named commanders can be turned.
- **The dossier:** a player-facing record of Queen-faction people and sites, with each entry carrying a confidence and an age. Unknown stays unknown. It is the mirror of the Queen's file (#196).
- **Gating:** what the dossier shows is bounded by intel gathered, nothing is free. This also gates the authored defection and turning events of curated commanders (see the cast canary issue): a commander can only be approached once the player holds the right intel.
- **Two-way:** the player can also feed *her* intel channel with deception (#118).

## Canary slice (definition of done)
One end-to-end loop: capture and interrogate an officer from the cast canary (the Drassen commander or a lieutenant), reveal one fact (for example the next commander's identity and trait or a garrison weakness), and show it in a minimal dossier entry with a confidence and an age.

## What

At native sizes (`>=1280x720`, the native map screen) the sector-load zoom-fade is invisible: it draws into the legacy frame buffer while the native map screen paints its own map canvas (`strategic-map` image) over the whole canvas area. The player sees a frozen map screen for the 2 s of the transition (and `ja2.debug("transition", t)` screenshots show the map screen, not the zoom). Same story for the pre-battle and laptop power up/down zooms when a native screen covers them.

Discovered while working on #159 (the transition is now drawn from pure progress and skips entirely when nobody can see it — but "someone is watching" is not the same as "the frames are visible").

## Evidence

`tests/e2e/manual/diag_loadscreen.lua` / `diag_transition.lua` at 1920x1080: after `ja2.debug("transition", 1.0)` (a black frame) the composed pixel at the centre is unchanged; at 640x480 (legacy UI) the zoom draws fine. Pre-existing: the old binary behaves the same.

## Options

- Zoom what the player is actually looking at: compose the current frame (native UI included), run the transition from that, and detach the native overlay for the duration.
- Or hide the native screen while the transition runs and let the legacy layer show it.
- Or make the transition a native-layer effect (zoom the map canvas element) and drop the legacy-layer one at native sizes.

## Definition of done

The transition is visible at 640x480 *and* at native sizes, with screenshot proof per AGENTS.md; `ja2.debug("transition", t)` captures it at every size.

issues.body:
## Context
Classic JA2 is a one-way ratchet: clear a town, hold it, collect mine income, buy gear, clear the next. Nothing pushes back, so the living-world work (Queen's Mind, reputation, named NPCs, militia, economy) would only decorate a loop the player already solved. Mercs are heroes: a fight has no clock, no lasting cost, and every enemy is an interchangeable body.

**Thesis.** Territory is a liability that pays rent; a raiding band is an asset that builds nothing. Governing earns steady cash, militia and facilities but costs upkeep, exposure and merc time. Raiding earns loot, intel, legend and delay on the Queen but has no safe base and no income. Neither dominates; the skilled play is a hybrid: hold one required HQ, raid out of it. A pure raider still needs that one base for inventory and management.

**Player-POV rules.** One readout per town ('how hard is it'), three verbs (Scout, Soften, Take), leads instead of menus, complexity under the hood, no new meters, and every mechanic must pass the 'if you...' test (one sentence starting with 'if you...').

Milestones: [Downed, not dead](https://github.com/adhikasp/ja2-stracciatella/milestone/19), [Raids & ambushes](https://github.com/adhikasp/ja2-stracciatella/milestone/20), [Stealth & disguise](https://github.com/adhikasp/ja2-stracciatella/milestone/21), [Taking a town](https://github.com/adhikasp/ja2-stracciatella/milestone/22), [Holding vs raiding](https://github.com/adhikasp/ja2-stracciatella/milestone/23). Build order: A, B, S, C, D. Design principles: `docs/plan/revamp-gameplay.md`.

- A hold-heavy run and a raid-heavy run (one HQ, no other territory) are both winnable, asserted in e2e (#257).

If a merc is shot to zero, they are downed, not dead; only you can finish someone.

issues.body:
## Context
An unknown person at night in plain clothes is assumed to be a townsperson. Enemies are not shoot-on-sight; they judge 'does this person fit?' from what they can see and shoot only at a clearly hostile sign. This builds the covert-ops disguise issue (#133) on the awareness meter (#222).

| Signal | Effect |
|---|---|
| Visible weapon (biggest) | A rifle in hand or slung is hostile on sight. Small items (pistol, knife) can be concealed in pockets and pass casual looks. |
| Clothing | Civilian clothes pass as locals; an enemy uniform as a soldier. Tiers: plain clothes, a local workman's outfit, a stolen uniform, forged papers from a contact (#241). |
| Time and place | A civilian outdoors at night is odd under curfew (#195); in a barracks or depot a civilian is out of place even in good clothes. |
| Behavior | Running, lingering near restricted spots, dragging bodies or standing over one raise suspicion; walking normally does not. |
| Known face | A merc seen by a survivor, or with high legend (#113) or a bounty (#195), is recognized more easily. Leaving witnesses burns that merc's cover. |
| Scrutiny | Distance lowers it; a checkpoint or conversation raises it; officers who know everyone are harder to fool. |

## Definition of done
- Suspicion feeds the awareness meter (#222) as a **slow fill**: an unknown face gets a curious look and maybe a challenge (show papers, bluff, move on) and escalates only on a hostile sign.
- A disguise breaks **locally**, for the witnesses, consistent with the carried alarm (#223).
- An attack from disguise gets the unaware bonus (#206).
- A cover tag on the merc shows the top reason it would break ('Cover: civilian. Rifle visible would break it'), so it is readable, not guessed.
- Limits: changing clothes costs AP; heavy gear and armor do not fit under civilian clothes; a group of armed-looking men is suspicious, so disguise is a one or two operative job with the squad waiting at the exfil.
- First cut: plain clothes and a stolen uniform; visible weapon, place and time, and behavior as signals.

## Builds on / depends on
- #133 (covert ops: disguise)
- #222
- #206
- #195 (curfew, bounties)
- #113 (legend)
- #200 (survivors leak a face)

## Player-facing sentence (the 'if you...' test)
If you walk at night in plain clothes with no weapon in sight, guards look but don't shoot; if you pull a rifle, they do.

## Open questions
O9: operatives only (default) or a whole squad? O10: how many outfits and signals in the first cut (default above).

## Test surface
Unit tests on the signal weights and the break rules; e2e: walk through a town at night in plain clothes unarmed (no escalation), then draw a rifle (escalation).
